title: A sick worker removes itself from the pool, then heals
goal: When a critical service stops on a worker, its health check makes it refuse new jobs by itself; Puppet then repairs the service and the worker takes jobs again, with no human decision.

steps.title: Baseline: both workers are healthy
steps.why: Each worker publishes NODE_IS_HEALTHY and the reason, as seen by the central manager.

command.stdout:
wn-01 true ok Unclaimed
wn-01 true ok Claimed
wn-01 true ok Claimed
wn-02 true ok Unclaimed
wn-02 true ok Claimed
wn-02 true ok Claimed

steps.title: Break a service on wn-01
steps.why: chronyd (time synchronisation) is one of the services a worker cannot run jobs without. An operator or a crash could stop it.

command.run: systemctl stop chronyd; echo "chronyd is now: $(systemctl is-active chronyd)"

steps.title: The worker declares itself sick
steps.why: The health check runs every 60 seconds. As soon as its output changes the startd publishes it to the collector.

after_wait.stdout:
wn-01 false service chronyd is not active
wn-02 true ok

steps.title: Submit 8 jobs of 25 seconds
steps.why: The queue holds more jobs than the healthy worker can run at once.

command.stdout:
Submitting job(s)........
8 job(s) submitted to cluster 3.

steps.title: Only the healthy worker runs jobs
steps.why: wn-01 is excluded by its own START expression: none of the running jobs is on it.

after_wait.run: condor_q -run -nobatch | grep -oE '@wn-[0-9]+' | sort | uniq -c; test $(condor_q -run -nobatch | grep -c '@wn-01') -eq 0

steps.title: Why an idle job waits
steps.why: condor_q -better-analyze separates 'the job asks too much' from 'the machines refuse the job': here the machines refuse.

command.run: condor_q -better-analyze $(condor_q -idle -af ClusterId ProcId | head -1 | tr ' ' .) 2>&1 | grep -E 'slots|Requirements expression'
command.stdout:
The Requirements expression for job 3.002 is
The Requirements expression for job 3.002 reduces to these conditions:
003.002:  Run analysis summary ignoring user priority.  Of 2 slots on 2 machines,
      0 slots are rejected by your job's requirements
      1 slots reject your job because of their own requirements
      0 slots match and are willing to run your job
      1 slots would match if drained

steps.title: Puppet repairs the service
steps.why: The next Puppet run notices chronyd is stopped, which is a drift from the desired state, and starts it.

command.run: /opt/puppetlabs/bin/puppet agent -t --detailed-exitcodes >/tmp/run.log 2>&1; rc=$?; grep -E 'Service.chronyd' /tmp/run.log | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | cut -c1-140; echo "puppet exit code: $rc (2 = changes applied)"; test $rc -eq 2
command.stdout:
Notice: /Stage[main]/Profile::Base/Service[chronyd]/ensure: ensure changed 'stopped' to 'running' (corrective)
Info: /Stage[main]/Profile::Base/Service[chronyd]: Unscheduling refresh on Service[chronyd]
puppet exit code: 2 (2 = changes applied)

steps.title: The worker declares itself healthy again
steps.why: The health check sees chronyd running, publishes True, and START accepts jobs again.

after_wait.stdout:
wn-01 true ok
wn-02 true ok
wn-02 true ok
wn-02 true ok

steps.title: Let the first batch finish
steps.why: So the next batch starts from an empty queue.

steps.title: A new batch runs on both workers
steps.why: The proof that wn-01 is back in service.

command.stdout:
Submitting job(s)........
8 job(s) submitted to cluster 4.
